back: The climate of a small area (city, valley, forest, lake shore) that differs from the surrounding region.
A city warmer than the surrounding countryside; intensity = urban temperature − rural temperature; strongest on calm, clear nights.

front: Causes of the urban heat island
back: Low-albedo surfaces that store heat, little evapotranspiration, building geometry trapping radiation, waste heat, and pollution.
Sea breeze: sea to land by day (land heats faster). Land breeze: land to sea at night (land cools faster).
Cold, dense air draining downslope at night; collects in valley bottoms to form frost hollows.
Warm air flowing up a heated slope during the day.
Cooler and more humid by day, warmer at night, less wind and a smaller temperature range than open ground.
The warmer zone on a mid-slope above the valley cold pool; better for frost-sensitive crops.
